evidence.source: 普及版 字通, via Kotobank
evidence.field: 字形 / 訓義 / 聲系
evidence.text: The entry analyzes 又 as a right hand and 口 as a ritual prayer vessel, interpreting the graph in a ritual context and associating later usage with assistance. It rejects the received Shuowen/Duan hand-and-mouth account as the original construction. It treats 又 as the initial graph and 右, 佑, and 祐 as later related graphs; this account does not establish 口 as a meaningless differentiating mark or 又 as a phonetic component within 右.
evidence.title: 右(ウ)とは？ 意味や使い方 - コトバンク

evidence.source: 精選版 日本国語大辞典, via Kotobank
evidence.text: The entry dates Japanese documentary use of 右 for a previously stated passage to the late eighth-century 万葉集, a right-side contest team to 898, and a directional example to 栄花物語 (circa 1028–1092). These are Japanese textual examples and do not date the Chinese graph’s origin or earliest sense. The same entry records later rank and political uses but does not establish their Chinese semantic chronology.
evidence.title: 右(ウ)とは？ 意味や使い方 - コトバンク

evidence.field: Scope and provenance of reconstruction table
evidence.text: The authors’ site identifies its downloadable reconstructions as supplementary materials for Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction (2014) and describes a list of nearly 5,000 reconstructed items. The exact entries for 又, 口, and 右 were not opened from the downloadable table in this research, so the supplied local table rows remain locally checked readings rather than independently verified external readings.
evidence.title: The Baxter-Sagart reconstruction of Old Chinese

evidence.field: OC / MC / Mandarin / gloss (sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv, character row 又)
evidence.text: The supplied exact local row gives 又: Mandarin yòu; Middle Chinese hjuwH; Old Chinese *[ɢ]ʷəʔ-s; ‘also, in addition’. The authors’ site confirms the relevant 2014 supplementary table exists, but its exact row was not externally inspected. The local reading is not evidence by itself that 又 is a phonetic component of 右.
evidence.title: The Baxter-Sagart reconstruction of Old Chinese

evidence.field: OC / MC / Mandarin / gloss (sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv, character row 口)
evidence.text: The supplied exact local row gives 口: Mandarin kǒu; Middle Chinese khuwX; Old Chinese *kʰˤ(r)oʔ; ‘mouth’. The exact reconstruction entry was not externally inspected, so this is a local table reading rather than an externally verified reading. It does not establish the role of 口 in 右.
evidence.title: The Baxter-Sagart reconstruction of Old Chinese

evidence.field: OC / MC / Mandarin / gloss (sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv, character rows 右)
evidence.text: The supplied local rows give 右: Mandarin yòu; MC hjuwX, OC *[ɢ]ʷəʔ, ‘right hand’; and MC hjuwH, OC *[ɢ]ʷəʔ-s (~ *m-qʷəʔ), ‘right hand’. Against 又’s supplied row (*[ɢ]ʷəʔ-s, MC hjuwH), the first 右 reading is similar in Old Chinese but differs in MC tone and reading form; the second has the same listed MC and OC form. These are distinct table readings and do not prove a sound-component role or a whole-graph loan. The exact rows were not externally fetched.
evidence.title: The Baxter-Sagart reconstruction of Old Chinese

evidence.field: kMandarin (sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt, character rows 又, 口, 右)
evidence.text: The supplied exact local kMandarin rows give 又 = yòu, 口 = kǒu, and 右 = yòu. The character-specific official Unihan pages for U+53C8, U+53E3, and U+53F3 could not be opened, so the local rows are not independently authenticated here as external readings. Unihan readings are modern metadata, not evidence for an ancient sound relationship.
evidence.title: Unicode Unihan character-specific records

evidence.text: The source presents the ritual-vessel analysis as a scholarly interpretation and separately catalogs assistance, right-hand/directional, favor, esteem, and banquet-related uses. Its Japanese lexicographic dates establish examples for Japanese usage only. It does not independently date the Chinese inscription examples or establish a chronological chain among direction, assistance, blessing, rank, west, and banquet use.

search_audit.outcome: Search returned competing explanations: 又 as an earlier whole graph with 口 added to distinguish it, and a ritual interpretation of 又 plus a vessel-like 口. Opened Kotobank and the official Baxter–Sagart supplementary-materials page. Exact Commons result surfaced but its page was inaccessible.

search_audit.query: Open Kotobank right entry, Baxter–Sagart supplementary materials, official Unihan records for U+53F3 U+53C8 U+53E3, exact Commons 右-seal.svg page and original SVG
search_audit.outcome: Kotobank and Baxter–Sagart site opened. All three official Unihan pages were inaccessible through the web tool. Commons page was inaccessible and direct SVG fetch failed; no image provenance or pixels verified.

gaps: The primary paleographic form sequence and a dated original inscription image were not inspected. The rival proposals—口 as a later graphic differentiator versus a meaningful ritual vessel—remain unresolved.

The official Baxter–Sagart supplementary site was inspected, but the exact downloadable table rows were not opened. Exact readings reported above are from the supplied local rows and are not externally authenticated in this run.
Official Unihan character-specific pages for 又, 口, and 右 were inaccessible. Their modern readings are reported only from the supplied local rows.

No evidence independently establishes 又 as a phonetic component within 右. A similar reconstruction can support comparison but does not establish component role; the whole-graph borrowing proposal also lacks independent evidence for the original object's name and sound.

Kotobank provides dates for Japanese textual examples, not for the earliest Chinese inscriptional senses. Earliest Chinese directional and assistance/blessing uses, graphic transition dates, and semantic links remain unestablished.
The Shuowen forms differ in component order, but no critical manuscript or primary witness was inspected to resolve whether textual corruption explains the variation.
The exact Commons File:右-seal.svg page and direct SVG could not be inspected; the manifest's public-domain lead and local image do not provide verified provenance, pixels, identity, or reuse terms.
